title: INTC Stock’s Next Boost Could Be Here: Report Says Intel May Land Korea's SK Hynix As Major Customer

questions.question: Will SK hynix select Intel Foundry as a supplier for HBM4E base dies by the end of TSMC’s fiscal 2026?
questions.why_it_matters: A confirmed selection would show that a major memory-chip maker is diversifying advanced HBM base-die production away from TSMC, potentially putting some future foundry revenue at risk and strengthening Intel Foundry’s competitive position. The article describes the selection as under consideration, not as a completed decision.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing TSM question tracks whether TSMC begins commercial production on its 2-nanometer process. A supplier selection for SK hynix’s HBM4E base dies is a separate customer and sourcing outcome: it could happen even if the 2-nanometer milestone’s answer stays unchanged.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check by January 31, 2027, an analyst check date at TSMC’s FY2026 year-end; the article states no decision date. Review announcements or other public disclosures from SK hynix, Intel, and TSMC, as well as relevant company filings, for confirmation that Intel Foundry has been selected as an HBM4E base-die supplier. The article reports consideration, not a finalized selection.

evidence.quote: Shares of Intel Corp. recovered slightly in overnight trading late Sunday after a report in South Korean media said that semiconductor giant SK Hynix is considering Intel Foundry as a supplier for the base dies used in its next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported potential sourcing decision is the core outcome to track. The article attributes the report to South Korean media and says SK hynix is considering Intel, not that it has selected Intel.
evidence.original_speaker: The article’s journalist, summarizing a report in South Korean media.

evidence.quote: If the reported talks materialize in a deal, it would give the U.S. chipmaker a major new customer as it seeks to revive its contract manufacturing business.
evidence.what_it_shows: A deal would be a meaningful customer win for Intel Foundry, supporting the investment significance of the supplier-selection outcome. The statement is conditional.

evidence.quote: The South Korean memory giant is reportedly looking to outsource some base-die production to Intel Foundry beginning with HBM4E, the seventh-generation HBM product, according to a report by Korean outlet Herald Economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported possibility concerns outsourced HBM4E base-die production specifically. “Some” production could indicate diversification rather than replacement of TSMC.
evidence.original_speaker: Herald Economy, as reported by the article.

evidence.quote: The move would diversify a supply chain that is currently heavily reliant on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC).
evidence.what_it_shows: The potential sourcing change could reduce reliance on TSMC, giving it a direct competitive and possible revenue implication. It remains a reported potential move.

evidence.quote: SK Hynix produced base dies internally for HBM3E but began working with TSMC on more advanced logic dies starting with HBM4. Its HBM4 uses a TSMC-produced base die based on a 12nm-class process.
evidence.what_it_shows: TSMC is the incumbent external supplier for HBM4 base dies, establishing the current position against which a potential HBM4E sourcing decision would be assessed.

evidence.quote: Industry sources cited by Herald Economy said TSMC’s HBM4 base die is estimated to cost three to four times more than an SK Hynix-produced core DRAM die.
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported cost comparison provides context for why SK hynix might consider changing or diversifying its sourcing. It is an estimate attributed to unnamed industry sources, not a confirmed cost or explanation of SK hynix’s decision.
evidence.original_speaker: Unnamed industry sources cited by Herald Economy.

evidence.quote: As HBM generations become more sophisticated, base-die costs are expected to rise further, while long-term supply agreements make it difficult for SK Hynix to simply pass higher manufacturing costs on to customers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Rising expected costs and difficulty passing them through could strengthen the incentive to seek another supplier. This is a reported industry rationale, not proof that SK hynix will select Intel.

evidence.quote: The potential foundry tie-up comes after recent speculation that SK Hynix could have a broader relationship with Intel.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article places the base-die possibility in the context of other reported relationship speculation, but this does not itself confirm the HBM4E supplier outcome.

evidence.quote: In July, reports said SK Hynix was among potential partners Intel was considering to help operate its delayed Ohio fab. SK Hynix denied pursuing an acquisition of the site, but separate reports said an operating partnership remained a possibility, although no formal negotiations had begun.
evidence.what_it_shows: This passage cautions that other reported Intel–SK hynix ties were speculative: SK hynix denied pursuing an acquisition, and no formal operating-partnership negotiations had begun. It does not establish negotiations or a decision on HBM4E base dies.
evidence.original_speaker: The article reports that SK hynix denied pursuing an acquisition; the other claims are attributed to reports.

evidence.quote: For Intel, an HBM base-die contract would help its foundry business attempt a turnaround after years of manufacturing setbacks.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article characterizes a contract as potentially relevant to Intel Foundry’s turnaround, underscoring that the sourcing outcome could matter competitively. It is conditional and does not quantify the contract’s value to TSMC or Intel.

evidence.quote: Intel has ramped its 18A process into high-volume production and is developing 14A as its first leading-edge node designed from the outset for external customers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Intel’s reported production progress and development plans provide competitive context for its effort to attract external foundry customers; they do not confirm that SK hynix has selected Intel for HBM4E.

evidence.quote: Intel Foundry, however, remains deeply loss-making, reporting a $2.1 billion operating loss in the second quarter of 2026 despite higher revenue.
evidence.what_it_shows: Intel Foundry’s reported loss highlights the financial importance of winning external business, while also showing that a possible contract would be only one part of its broader financial position.
evidence.original_speaker: The article’s journalist, citing Intel Foundry’s second-quarter 2026 result.

questions_written.question: Will SK hynix select Intel Foundry as a supplier for HBM4E base dies by the end of TSMC’s fiscal 2026?

article:
In July, reports said SK hynix was among potential partners Intel was considering to help operate its delayed Ohio fab, although SK Hynix denied the reports.
Stocktwits sentiment for INTC was ‘bullish’ on Sunday.
Shares of Intel Corp. recovered slightly in overnight trading late Sunday after a report in South Korean media said that semiconductor giant SK Hynix is considering Intel Foundry as a supplier for the base dies used in its next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
If the reported talks materialize in a deal, it would give the U.S. chipmaker a major new customer as it seeks to revive its contract manufacturing business.
Intel shares were down 0.5% at the time of writing, recovering from a nearly 2% drop about an hour earlier. SK Hynix’s U.S.-listed shares were down 1.5%.
The South Korean memory giant is reportedly looking to outsource some base-die production to Intel Foundry beginning with HBM4E, the seventh-generation HBM product, according to a report by Korean outlet Herald Economy. The move would diversify a supply chain that is currently heavily reliant on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC).
The base die sits at the bottom of an HBM stack and handles logic, control, and high-speed connectivity between the memory stack and processors such as GPUs. SK Hynix produced base dies internally for HBM3E but began working with TSMC on more advanced logic dies starting with HBM4. Its HBM4 uses a TSMC-produced base die based on a 12nm-class process.
Industry sources cited by Herald Economy said TSMC’s HBM4 base die is estimated to cost three to four times more than an SK Hynix-produced core DRAM die. As HBM generations become more sophisticated, base-die costs are expected to rise further, while long-term supply agreements make it difficult for SK Hynix to simply pass higher manufacturing costs on to customers.
The potential foundry tie-up comes after recent speculation that SK Hynix could have a broader relationship with Intel. In July, reports said SK Hynix was among potential partners Intel was considering to help operate its delayed Ohio fab. SK Hynix denied pursuing an acquisition of the site, but separate reports said an operating partnership remained a possibility, although no formal negotiations had begun.
The companies already have a significant history together. In 2020, Intel agreed to sell its NAND and SSD business and Dalian memory facility to SK Hynix for $9 billion, with the transaction subsequently completed.
For Intel, an HBM base-die contract would help its foundry business attempt a turnaround after years of manufacturing setbacks. Intel has ramped its 18A process into high-volume production and is developing 14A as its first leading-edge node designed from the outset for external customers.
Intel Foundry, however, remains deeply loss-making, reporting a $2.1 billion operating loss in the second quarter of 2026 despite higher revenue.
INTC Stock: What Do Retail Traders Feel?
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for INTC climbed over the past week and was ‘bullish’ as of late Sunday, with the ticker trending among the top five equities at the time of writing.
“$INTC Buy the dip. Trump and Pelosi both in. Rare event,” a trader wrote , referring to the President’s and former House Speaker’s stakes in the chipmaker.
Another wrote: “$INTC Production deal with SK Hynix. Nice. Should be good enough news to give us a -10 percent day tomorrow.”
One trader expressed a bit of caution: “BUY THE RUMOR, SELL THE NEWS… ‘Sk Hynix CONSIDERING’ IMO price will rally and when the news drops about the deal its time to SELL it.”
Intel stock has lost steam in recent months after a sharp rally earlier this year. Shares are down nearly 1% in August after an over 35% drop in the previous month, although they remain 143% higher year to date.
